newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Corporate troubles seen depressing Seoul stocks.
newsitem.headline: Corporate troubles seen depressing Seoul stocks.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to remain in the doldrums on Wednesday because of investors' jitters about more corporate failures, brokers said.
They said financial woes suffered by the Kia and Jinro groups and rumours of cash flow problems into Ssangyong Group would continue to plague the wobbly stock market.

"Further consolidation looks inevitable. There is no favourable news to turn the market around," said Kim Dae-hee at LG Securities. "Ssangyong's denial of trouble yesterday failed to soothe investor fears and many will stay on the sidelines."
The stock index fell 14.95 points to 725.98 on Tuesday.
Brokers forecast a mild technical rebound following recent sharp declines but they said the rises would be limited.
"The index is likely to retreat soon to the 710 level," Kim said.
A lukewarm attitude by foreign investors also chilled investor sentiment, brokers said.
